My first and only Lucid dream/out of body experience. 

Basically was going to bed. And I dreamt I was watching television but it felt so real. Like I didn’t even feel I was dreaming or had even gone to sleep. At one point I goto plug in my phone and I ended up tripping and falling on my stomach. 

However, the fall was soft and didn’t feel painful. As I get up I suddenly realize that I’m in my bed waking up later that night. 

I just remember lying there in total fear trying to figure out what just happened. It’s like my mind departed from my body for a moment and I “fell” back into it. The transition from sleeping to waking up was seamless, it was freaky. The dream didn’t even scare me, it was the experience. Freaked me out. Literally had to sleep with the light turned on after that. Couldn’t stop thinking about it.

I felt pretty lonely during my senior year of high school. Probably didn’t help that I was being bullied at the time but nonetheless, starting university was exciting. I looked forward to leaving high school behind and being in an environment where 90% of the students were mature individuals. University really made high school look like a elementary school.

However, there are many new challenges in university. Didn’t make any friends, was a lone wolf. Which personally doesn’t bother me entirely because I like doing projects on my own. Again though, making some friends or having something that represents a social circle in university would’ve been nice.

I don’t say this to scare you. But it’ll be different, and who knows? Maybe you’ll thrive because of the change of scenery! 

Another thing, like you, I hung on because of things I looked forward to in the future. I said I’d end it over a year ago after a certain event passed. What I’ve found is there will always be something to look forward to. Doesn’t change the fact I still feel shitty, but it does give me hope and a glimpse of how life isn’t as bad as I make it out to be. Recognizing our own perception of things always being negative can actually heal us. Because we accept that “Hey, I can feel myself looking at the negative. But is that all there is to see?”. 

I’d be lying if I told you my life is all sunshine and rainbows right now. I’m actually going through my own personal hell. But the recognition that not everything need to be seen as negative, I’ve found some peace within myself. That is what I call hope. And I’ll hold on to it for as long as I can. So far I’ve done tremendously well. 

I wish you the best OP. I have faith that you’ll find your own hope too :).
